key_insight: The paper introduces a practical automated annotation system that finds rare delayed and false AEB events by combining imbalance-aware synthetic data generation with noise suppression for mislabeled majority samples.
engineering_relevance: For autonomous braking systems, this reduces costly manual review while improving the quality of critical edge-case labels needed to optimize safety and trigger performance.
method: Synthesizes realistic minority examples by editing focal-target attributes, transplanting ego-vehicle dynamics, and masking non-focal agents.
Suppresses asymmetric label noise with stable hardness estimation and a probe-guided adaptive threshold to filter mislabeled true-trigger samples.
Deploys the model in a full-stack production annotation pipeline for daily AEB event triage.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an 80% recall improvement for delayed/false triggers and a 50% reduction in manual workload in production use.
watch_item: Results depend on the realism of synthetic augmentation and the reliability of noise filtering, so performance may vary when sensor distributions or trigger definitions change.
paper_title: Learning to Annotate Delayed and False AEB Events: A Practical System for Extreme Class Imbalance and Asymmetric Label Noise
